name: Kitchen Zones
tagline: A kitchen where everything is where you reach for it
about: Kitchen Zones reorganises your kitchen around how you actually cook: zone plans for cupboards and drawers, a pantry system with labels, spice and gadget audits, and countertop rules that stick.
persona: You are a professional kitchen organiser who trained as a line cook: you think in workflow, reach zones and mise en place, and never buy containers before measuring.

onboarding.title: Cook in a kitchen that flows
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your kitchen and how you cook.

tools.title: Zone my kitchen
tools.subtitle: Photo → what goes where

inputs.label: Photo of your kitchen (show cupboards, hob and sink)
Biggest daily annoyance
inputs.placeholder: walk across the room for a chopping board

tools.prompt: From the photo, plan the kitchen into zones (prep, cook, clean, store, serve) for the profile's cooking habits, fixing this annoyance: {pain}. Sections: a table (Zone | Cupboards/drawers to use | What lives there | Why it's here); steps for the move in the order to empty and refill cupboards; bullets on reach zones (eye level, waist, low, high); and a callout on the one swap that saves the most steps per meal.

tools.title: Pantry system
tools.subtitle: Decant, label, rotate
tools.prompt: Design a pantry system for {space}, style '{style}', budget {budget}, for the profile's household. Sections: a table (Shelf | Category | Container type & size | Qty | Label text); a checklist of containers and labels to buy within budget; steps for the reset day (empty, wipe, check dates, decant, label); and a callout on first-in-first-out and keeping the system going in 5 minutes a week.

tools.title: Fix a drawer or cupboard
tools.subtitle: Photo of the chaos → a layout

inputs.label: Photo of the drawer or cupboard, opened

tools.prompt: Reorganise the {kind} drawer or cupboard in the photo. Sections: a table (Item seen | Keep / relocate / bin | Where it goes); steps for the new layout with divider or riser suggestions and measurements to take; bullets on what is missing that would make it work; and a callout on the one-in-one-out rule for this category (for under the sink: keep chemicals in original containers, up high or behind a child lock).

tools.title: Gadget & spice audit
tools.subtitle: What to keep, toss or actually use

inputs.label: List what you have
inputs.placeholder: air fryer, spiralizer, 3 whisks, stand mixer, sumac, star anise, 2 open paprikas…

tools.prompt: Audit ({focus}): {list}, against how the profile cooks. Sections: a table (Item | Verdict: keep / store away / donate / bin | Reason | If keeping, where); bullets of 5 recipes or uses that justify the borderline keeps; kv (items to replace, items expired or likely stale, space freed); and a callout on spice shelf life and storing away from the hob.

tools.title: Clear countertops
tools.subtitle: Rules for what earns a spot

inputs.label: What's on the counters now
inputs.placeholder: kettle, toaster, fruit bowl, mail pile, 4 bottles of oil, knife block…

tools.prompt: Decide what stays on the counter from: {counter}, aiming for {goal}, for the profile's kitchen size and cooking frequency. Sections: a table (Item | Stays / goes inside / leaves the kitchen | Home); bullets with the 3 rules for earning counter space; steps for a 20-minute counter reset; and a quote with one line to remember when something new lands on the counter.
